ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every UBO, director, and authorized signatory against the Taiwan Financial Supervisory Commission's AML/CFT sanctions lists, the PRC Ministry of Public Security's politically exposed person (PEP) and terrorist lists, the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions, and EU restrictive measures. Each relationship must undergo ongoing risk-based due diligence, with enhanced scrutiny for PEPs, their family members and close associates, and any individual with source-of-wealth inconsistencies. Cross-border payment rails such as Wise B2B and bank wires trigger additional transaction monitoring. Any sanctions match requires immediate suspension of the application, filing with Taiwan's Financial Reporting Center for Economic Crime, and a freeze of funds or assets connected to the flagged person, followed by a legal counsel incident report.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Taiwan (R.O.C.) Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) - Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Approval System (Company Registration Online Application; Department of Commerce, MOEA)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be formed in statutory Chinese characters; an English trade name may be additionally registered as an alternate but the Chinese name remains the controlling legal identifier. The four-tier naming convention requires (1) a distinctive trade name, (2) a description of the actual business scope, (3) an organization type suffix such as Limited, Limited Liability Company or Co., Ltd., and (4) any mandatory indication of foreign or mainland Chinese investment. Phonetic transliteration from English to Mandarin is required when the trade name contains a foreign word; English-only names are not permitted as the legal name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Taiwan (as a standalone name element without ministerial approval)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A rejected name application may be contested by filing a written objection with the MOEA Department of Commerce within 30 days of receiving the rejection, citing Article 18 of the Company Act or the applicable provisions of the Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Approval Regulations. The objection must include the rejected Chinese name, the registered business scope, and a comparative analysis demonstrating that no same-industry company has a confusingly similar name. If the objection is dismissed, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the Administrative Appeals Commission of the Executive Yuan within 30 days after the dismissal, and thereafter may initiate administrative litigation in the Taipei High Administrative Court. A parallel re-application with a more distinctive token, such as adding a geographic qualifier or an operational descriptor, is strongly recommended to avoid delay. The initial reservation may be extended once for an additional 180 days before expiration by filing a continuation request and paying the required fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Taiwan's Company Act requires a registered office within Taiwan, but does not absolutely outlaw a virtual office. However, the tax authority and Taiwan banks generally reject a mere commercial mailbox for an ISIC 7020 consultancy because they require demonstrable physical business presence, local substantive employees, and operational capacity. A virtual office is permissible only if it includes a dedicated registered agent, a physical meeting room, a workable mailbox, and a lease of at least one year with evidence of utility usage; even then, the financial institution may impose enhanced due diligence and request documentary proof of actual business operations during the initial account opening phase.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: 25% probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first year for a standard consultancy with a physical office; 55% probability if a virtual office is used; and 70% probability if cross-border payment traffic is high without local staff. Checklist: (1) confirm the company nameplate is posted at the registered address; (2) inspect the lease agreement and utility bills; (3) interview at least one full-time local employee; (4) review minutes of board meetings physically held on-site; (5) verify local tax filings and social security contributions. Failure to pass an inspection can trigger deregistration, administrative fines, and bank account freezing.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Act of Taiwan, Articles 18, 128-129, 156, 161-164, 172, 192, 208 and 218; Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals, Articles 5, 7, 8 and 10; Company Registration Regulations and related MOEA implementation rules
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan (Company Registration Division)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Establishment Registration Application Form together with duly adopted Articles of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Taiwan Company Act imposes no statutory minimum paid-up capital for a company limited by shares. However, under the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals, the joint venture capital must be remitted into a Taiwan-registered bank account opened in the company's name and verified by a Taiwan-licensed certified public accountant; no blocked escrow account is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF OVERSEAS MARKET ENTRY CONSULTING CO., LTD. ADOPTED ON [DATE] BY UNANIMOUS CONSENT OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS IN ACCORDANCE WITH ARTICLES 192 AND 208 OF THE COMPANY ACT OF TAIWAN. RESOLVED: (1) The incorporation of the Company as a company limited by shares under the laws of Taiwan is hereby ratified and confirmed, and the Articles of Incorporation as executed by the incorporating shareholders and filed with the Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs, are adopted as the governance charter of the Company. (2) The authorized share capital of the Company is [N] ordinary shares with a par value of NT$[X] per share; the board ratifies the issuance and subscription of all shares to the joint venture parties; and the board confirms that the initial paid-in capital of NT$[Y] has been contributed, received, and credited to the Company's temporary corporate bank account in accordance with the capital verification report of the Company's independent certified public accountant. (3) The registered office of the Company shall be situated at [ADDRESS]; the board authorizes the President and any director, individually, to execute or cause to be executed any lease, utility, insurance, municipal registration, and postal documents necessary to establish and maintain the registered office. (4) The board authorizes the opening of operating, foreign-currency, and deposit accounts with [BANK] in Taiwan and appoints [NAME] and [NAME], acting jointly or severally, as signatories and authorized representatives with full authority to open, operate, endorse, sign, close, and manage those accounts, including applying for wire transfers, online banking, and Wise/B2B payment services. (5) The following statutory officers are duly appointed: Chairperson [NAME]; General Manager/President [NAME]; Company Secretary [NAME]; and Chief Financial Officer [NAME], each to serve at the pleasure of the board and with the powers and duties conferred by the Company Act and the Company's internal control procedures. (6) The board directs the President and the Company Secretary to file the incorporation registration package with the Department of Commerce, to engage a certified public accountant for any required capital verification, to complete tax and labor registrations, and to take all further actions necessary to declare this resolution effective immediately. This resolution may be executed in one or more counterparts and is binding on the Company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Name Reservation and Foreign Investment Screening Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEAIC), Taiwan; Company Name and Business Scope Pre-approval System, Department of Commerce, MOEA
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an online foreign investment application with the Investment Commission using the prescribed statutory form, naming the Chinese and English company, ISIC 7020 business scope, shareholding percentages, capital remittance schedule, and the identity/residency documents of directors. In parallel, reserve the company name and pre-audit the business scope through the Department of Commerce online platform. The applicant must upload a board/shareholder authorization letter from the Chinese parent or joint venture party and a bank reference. The Investment Commission will screen for restricted sectors under the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals and issue an investment approval letter. No business may commence before company registration approval.
required_dossiers: Investment Commission foreign investment application form
Company name and business scope pre-approval form
Chinese and English company name choices
Draft Articles of Incorporation and business plan
Shareholder and director identity documents and passport copies
Board/shareholder authorization resolution of the Chinese parent company
Bank reference or proof of funding source
Power of attorney in favor of the local incorporation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Investment Commission issues a clarification notice or suspends the application, respond within 14 days with an amended scope, updated capital schedule, or corrected ownership chart. A rejection may be cured by reducing the proposed shareholding below sensitive thresholds or deleting restricted business descriptors. A name refusal requires selection of a new name and immediate online re-application through the same pre-approval workflow.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Constitutional Documents and First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public and Taiwan-licensed certified public accountant engaged by the formation counsel; no registry filing at this stage
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After investment approval, convene the incorporating shareholders and first board of directors. Prepare the Articles of Incorporation, share subscription ledger, and the pro-forma first board resolution approving the subscribed capital, banking authorization, registered office, and statutory officer appointments. All directors must execute the resolution and articles; signatures should be witnessed by a notary public if required by the bank or the registered office landlord. A Taiwan-licensed CPA must issue a capital verification report based on remittance into a temporary bank account opened in the company's name. Although Taiwan law does not universally require notarization of articles, notarization is recommended when foreign shareholders will rely on the documents abroad.
required_dossiers: Directors' consent letters and identity documents
Notarized power of attorney, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the reviewing bank or foreign investor queries the executions, correct the signature page and have the same or a substituted director re-execute before a notary public. Any mismatch between the approved investment letter and the Articles, particularly with respect to paid-in capital or business scope, must be cured by amending the Articles and filing a supplemental Investment Commission application before proceeding.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Registration Filing with Department of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan (MOEA Company Registration Online Platform)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete incorporation package through the MOEA Company Registration Online Platform or in person at the designated central registry. The registry verifies that the Articles comply with the Company Act, the name is not confusingly similar, the paid-in capital is verifiable, and the directors and statutory representative meet legal requirements. Attach the CPA capital verification report or bank certificate, proof of payment of the registration fee, and the Investment Commission approval. The registry will issue the Company Registration Certificate and a Unified Business Number. This constitutes the legal existence of the company. After issuance, obtain the company seal and establish the permanent corporate bank accounts.
required_dossiers: Capital verification report and bank statement
Registered office consent or lease document
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a query or suspension, cure the stated deficiencies within 15 days by filing supplementary documents and paying a refiling fee if the case is withdrawn. For capital verification defects, obtain an updated CPA report; for name confusion, submit a newly reserved name and amend the Articles accordingly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax, Labor, and Operational Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau (Ministry of Finance, Taiwan); local municipal business office; Bureau of Labor Insurance; National Health Insurance Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Company Registration Certificate, complete tax registration to obtain the Tax ID Card and Uniform Invoice Number, register the leased office with the local municipality if applicable, and enroll the company for labor insurance, pension, and national health insurance. For an ISIC 7020 cross-border consultancy, confirm that outward services are reported and that export-of-services zero-rated VAT treatment is claimed where supported by documentary evidence. Establish the permanent corporate bank account and validate the Wise/B2B payment rails with the bank's compliance officer. No industrial operating license is required for this pure consultancy business.
required_dossiers: Directors' and employees' identity and qualification documents
Labor insurance and health insurance enrollment forms
Corporate bank account opening forms and company seal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a tax or labor authority rejects the registration due to incomplete information, cure the data through the e-government portal and resubmit within the demand notice window. For discrepancies between the registry file and tax file, file an expedited correction and re-registration with the relevant bureau, attaching the board resolution and Company Registration Certificate.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - no industrial licensing board or municipal agency is engaged because ISIC 7020 is a pure management consultancy with no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operations.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no operational or manufacturing permit is required under Taiwan law for ISIC 7020 foreign market entry consultancy services.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - Environmental Protection Administration (EPA), Taiwan has no regulatory nexus.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - no full EIA report, environmental registration, or pollution control permit is required for a consultancy office.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no registered stationary source; zero wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste discharge thresholds apply because there is no manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing activity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no Civil Defense fire safety permit, structural load inspection, or occupational safety clearance is required for a pure ISIC 7020 consultancy office; the leased premises must nevertheless comply with general municipal building and fire safety codes.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Taxation Administration, Ministry of Finance (Taiwan); local enforcement by the National Taxation Bureau in the relevant tax district; electronic portal: Tax Information Portal at https://www.etax.nat.gov.tw and Electronic Tax Filing and Payment System at https://tax.nat.gov.tw.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-invested profit-seeking enterprise such as CN_JV_LTD: (1) obtain foreign-investment approval from the Investment Commission of the Ministry of Economic Affairs; (2) complete the profit-seeking enterprise registration and company registration with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and the local municipal/county authority; (3) file the prescribed tax registration application with the National Taxation Bureau where the business office is situated, attaching the approval certificate, certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, proof of business address, and identification and seal of the responsible person (and, if required, the local tax representative); (4) receive the Unified Business Number, the statutory tax identification number for income tax, business tax, uniform-invoice procurement, and customs declaration linkage; (5) elect electronic submission and e-invoice transmission on the Integrated Tax Portal after issuance of the Unified Business Number. For a foreign non-resident entity without a fixed place of business but making taxable Taiwanese-source sales or cross-border e-commerce sales, the foreign entity must register with the National Taxation Bureau itself or through an appointed local tax representative, using its foreign incorporation evidence, power of attorney, and a statement identifying the tax agent; the registration becomes effective when taxable Taiwanese-source revenue starts. No minimum statutory capital is required for the TIN, but tax registration cannot be completed before the underlying business registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Taiwan does not offer check-the-box, pass-through, or hybrid mismatch elections; the Sino-foreign equity joint venture is statutorily classified as a Taiwan profit-seeking enterprise and is subject to entity-level taxation on Taiwan-source income.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold for resident profit-seeking enterprises; every taxable business must complete business-tax registration before commencing operations. Small-scale businesses with monthly taxable sales at or below NT$200,000 remain registered but pay the reduced 1% non-value-added business tax. A foreign non-resident supplier of cross-border electronic services selling more than NT$480,000 per year to Taiwan individuals must register for business tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan mandates the issuance of Uniform Invoices for taxable sales. Electronic Uniform Invoices (cloud invoices) are issued through a Ministry-of-Finance-certified turnkey system or software integrator, using the statutory XML/JSON schema, digital certificates, and TLS transmission; invoice data is transmitted to the Ministry of Finance Cloud Invoice Database for validation, duplicate-issue detection, and anti-fraud monitoring. Printed electronic invoices must bear the 2D/QR barcode and random anti-counterfeit number. This is not a real-time government pre-clearance regime; however, invoice issuance, allowance, voidance, and monthly/quarterly Business Tax return declarations are automatically reconciled, and discrepancies trigger notices and penalties under the Business Tax Act.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 7 of the Business Tax Act, 0% VAT treatment applies to: (1) goods physically exported from Taiwan with customs clearance; (2) services sold by a Taiwan business to a wholly foreign client where the services are used or enjoyed outside Taiwan; (3) international transport and cross-border ancillary services; and (4) qualifying offshore digital or consultancy services. For an ISIC 7020 overseas market-entry consultancy, the service contract, feasibility and regulatory-licensing reports, the client's overseas business address, and foreign-currency invoices must evidence that the benefit of the consulting service lies outside Taiwan. The exporter then shows no output business tax on the transaction and claims credits for input business tax on related purchases; any residual input-credit refund is applied through the monthly/quarterly Business Tax return.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Entry) approved by Taiwan Customs Administration
Ocean Bill of Lading or international airway bill showing goods left Taiwan customs territory
Inward Remittance Certificate / Certificate of Foreign Exchange Settlement issued by an authorized foreign-exchange bank
For services: signed engagement contract, market-entry feasibility report, and payment records establishing the foreign client's offshore use
Foreign-exchange repatriation statement showing export/service proceeds were collected by the Taiwan entity
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Taxation Bureau reconciles Business Tax returns against customs export records, foreign-exchange settlement statements, and Cloud Invoice Database data. If the zero-rating claim is not substantiated, the gross consideration is assessed at 5% business tax, overdue interest is added, and administrative fines are imposed under Articles 51 and 52 of the Business Tax Act. Known forgery of customs documents or foreign-exchange certificates, sham offshore structures, or deliberate mischaracterization of domestic consultancy services as foreign use triggers criminal liability under Article 41, retroactive reassessment within the seven-year statutory assessment period, loss of refund entitlement, and seizure of assets/inventory where evasion is established. Export proceeds that are not repatriated within 180 days, absent central-bank approval for an extension, will normally cause the zero-rated export status to be denied.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan), together with the Ministry of Economic Affairs, Investment Commission, and the Banking Bureau of the Financial Supervisory Commission for applicable investment, banking, and cross-Strait controls
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Taiwan dollar is generally convertible for current-account transactions. Taiwan does not operate a general exchange-control regime requiring prior approval for ordinary trade receipts, service payments, dividends, interest, or other legitimate current-account remittances, subject to bank reporting, documentary verification, anti-money-laundering controls, tax compliance, and applicable foreign-exchange declaration thresholds. Capital-account transactions are more regulated. Corporate investments, outward investments, foreign borrowing, guarantees, securities transactions, and transactions involving mainland China may require prior approval, registration, declaration, or compliance with sectoral and cross-Strait restrictions. Profit remittance should be supported by audited or approved financial statements, shareholder or board resolutions, evidence of distributable profits, withholding-tax filings or tax clearance, and proof of the underlying investment. A China-based Sino-foreign equity joint venture must separately comply with Mainland China foreign-exchange, tax, dividend-distribution, and cross-border payment rules. Direct or indirect payments involving Taiwan and Mainland China require enhanced bank review under applicable cross-Strait regulations and may be prohibited where the underlying activity, counterparty, route, or beneficial ownership is restricted.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Taiwan has no general statutory rule requiring exporters to surrender all export proceeds to the Central Bank or convert them into New Taiwan dollars at a fixed ratio. Export proceeds may generally be retained in foreign-currency accounts or converted through authorized foreign-exchange banks. Banks require customs or commercial documentation, invoices, contracts, shipping records, and transaction-purpose information, and report or process qualifying foreign-exchange transactions under Central Bank rules. No universal export-proceeds conversion deadline or mandatory conversion percentage should be represented without confirming the current bank-specific and transaction-specific rule. For Mainland China operations, export receipts and foreign-exchange settlement are governed separately by the State Administration of Foreign Exchange and related Mainland rules; the applicable entity, export location, customs declaration, account type, and payment purpose determine repatriation, settlement, and documentation requirements.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for supplemental collections and payments; low as the sole treasury bank. An offshore electronic-money institution or payment institution, including Wise Business where the entity and use case are accepted, does not replace a Taiwan-authorized bank account, a regulated capital account, or any required Mainland China foreign-exchange channel. Availability depends on entity incorporation location, directors, beneficial owners, business activity, currencies, payment corridors, sanctions screening, and platform policy. Wise B2B should be treated as a payment service rather than a guaranteed bank-wire substitute. It may not support capital injections, shareholder funding, escrow, restricted cross-Strait settlements, regulated investment flows, cash deposits, documentary trade finance, or all Taiwan-dollar functions. Use a licensed Taiwan bank for registered capital, tax payments, payroll, dividend remittances, foreign-exchange declarations, and high-value or sensitive transactions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Taiwan banks may permit remote or representative-assisted onboarding for certain corporate customers, but they retain discretion to require an in-person interview, notarized or apostilled documents, local representative attendance, specimen-signature verification, video identification, or a branch visit. Physical attendance is more likely where the entity has foreign or Mainland Chinese shareholders, cross-Strait ownership, complex beneficial ownership, newly incorporated status, no local operating history, high expected transaction volumes, or sensitive payment corridors. Mainland China bank onboarding for the Sino-foreign equity joint venture is governed by Mainland bank and foreign-exchange requirements and commonly requires original corporate documents, legal-representative verification, tax and registration records, and bank interviews. Remote opening should not be assumed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear relationship between the China-based Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture, the Taiwan jurisdiction, and the proposed account-opening entity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified business registration and articles of association; joint-venture contract; shareholder register; organization chart; legal-entity and tax-residency map; explanation of the Taiwan operating or payment nexus; board resolutions; authorized-signatory list; and legal memorandum describing cross-Strait transaction permissibility

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership involving Mainland China, Taiwan, nominee shareholders, state-linked entities, or layered holding companies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ownership chart to ultimate natural-person or publicly listed-parent level; passports and residential evidence for controlling persons; shareholder certificates; incorporation records for every intermediate entity; declarations of no nominee ownership; sanctions and politically exposed person screening results; and source-of-wealth statements

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection or shareholder funding that is inconsistent with registered capital, investment approval, foreign-exchange registration, or the stated corporate purpose
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Joint-venture approval or registration materials; capital contribution schedule; shareholder resolution; subscription agreement; bank remittance instructions; source-of-funds evidence; audited financial statements of the investor; tax residency certificates; purpose code; and confirmation from the receiving bank or authorized foreign-exchange bank

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Consulting payments described as market-entry or licensing assistance without a defined deliverable, customer, territory, or regulatory scope
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed master services agreement; statement of work; invoices; deliverables; engagement chronology; customer due diligence; proof of service performance; employee or contractor records; pricing rationale; licensing and regulatory analysis; and confirmation that no unlicensed agency, brokerage, public-affairs, legal, or regulated financial activity is being performed

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payments, pass-through receipts, unrelated payer names, or payment flows inconsistent with the contracting party
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Tri-party agreement or payment assignment; beneficial-owner explanation; commercial invoices; contract chain; board approval; payer and beneficiary KYC; rationale for third-party settlement; bank correspondence; and written confirmation that the arrangement is not money transmission, trade-based money laundering, or sanctions evasion

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value, round-number, rapid in-and-out, or multi-currency transactions inconsistent with the stated low-risk consultancy profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Rolling 12-month cash-flow forecast; transaction-volume matrix; expected counterparties and countries; contract pipeline; revenue model; payroll and operating-cost budget; treasury policy; reconciliation procedures; and documented escalation controls for unusual activity

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments involving Mainland China and Taiwan that may implicate cross-Strait restrictions, prohibited industries, restricted counterparties, or an impermissible payment route
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty ownership and location report; underlying contracts; goods or services description; end-use and end-customer statements; applicable Investment Commission or other approvals; sanctions and export-control screening; authorized-bank confirmation; legal analysis of cross-Strait permissions; and evidence that the payment does not bypass required Mainland or Taiwan channels

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of offshore fintech accounts as the principal operating account or for capital, tax, payroll, escrow, or regulated settlement functions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Licensed-provider status; account terms; permitted-use analysis; segregation of operating and capital funds; domestic bank account evidence; transaction-routing policy; reconciliation controls; tax-payment process; and written confirmation from the provider that the proposed currencies, corridors, and customer activities are supported

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete tax, accounting, or profit-remittance records
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Tax registration; VAT or business-tax filings where applicable; audited financial statements; board and shareholder dividend resolutions; retained-earnings reconciliation; withholding-tax computation; tax payment receipts or clearance; transfer-pricing documentation; and evidence of distributable profits

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route capital through an authorized Taiwan or Mainland China bank account designated for the relevant investment or capital purpose; do not use a personal account, unrelated third-party account, or offshore EMI wallet. The remittance instruction should identify the investor, recipient, legal entity, capital contribution or shareholder-loan purpose, currency, amount, and underlying agreement. Attach the joint-venture contract, corporate registration, capital subscription or loan agreement, shareholder resolution, source-of-funds evidence, tax and foreign-exchange registration or approval documents, and bank-required purpose code. The receiving bank should validate the investor, beneficial owner, source of funds, registered capital or permitted debt capacity, and whether the transaction is legally permitted across the relevant China-Taiwan corridor. Reconcile the received amount to the capital ledger and regulatory filings before deployment.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use authorized bank transfers for ordinary consulting expenses, supplier payments, payroll, taxes, and legitimate cross-border services. A SWIFT MT103 or equivalent customer credit transfer is appropriate for transparent bilateral settlement and should include complete originator, beneficiary, invoice, contract, purpose, and intermediary-bank information. Use a commercial letter of credit, standby letter of credit, documentary collection, or bank guarantee only where commercially justified and supported by the underlying contract; documentary trade instruments are generally unnecessary for pure consultancy services unless a bank requires security or staged payment. Retain invoices, service acceptance evidence, tax documents, contracts, sanctions screening, and payment reconciliations. Do not split transactions to avoid reporting thresholds or route payments through unrelated jurisdictions. Mainland China payments must use an authorized Mainland channel and comply with SAFE, tax, banking, and cross-Strait requirements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with an authorized Taiwan or Mainland China bank, supported by a documented underlying exposure and subject to bank suitability, tenor, collateral, and reporting requirements

Non-deliverable forwards where offered by an authorized institution and legally available for the relevant currency and customer; NDFs should be used only for genuine exposure management and not for speculative trading

Currency swaps or cross-currency swaps with an authorized bank for documented funding or currency-mismatch exposures, subject to master documentation, counterparty limits, valuation, collateral, and accounting controls
Foreign-exchange options or collars, where permitted and approved by the bank, with documented exposure, suitability assessment, premium and worst-case-loss analysis

Natural hedging through matching currency receipts and expenditures, foreign-currency cash pooling where legally available, and timing or netting arrangements supported by contracts and authorized-bank procedures

Prohibited or high-risk practices include unlicensed derivatives dealing, speculative leveraged positions, informal netting, personal-account hedging, undocumented related-party swaps, and use of offshore platforms that are not authorized for the entity or transaction

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Withholding Tax Certificate Filing (扣繳憑單申報)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By January 31 of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts a surcharge up to 20% of the uncollected/withholding amount; intentional evasion may lead to a tax audit and criminal referral for responsible persons.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Company Information and Beneficial Ownership Report (每年公司資訊申報)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Commercial Registration Portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By March 31 each year (covering the previous fiscal year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance exposes the company and responsible officer to fines of TWD 10,000–500,000; repeated violations may be penalized up to TWD 5,000,000 and lead to administrative deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (營利事業所得稅結算申報)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By May 31 of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a penalty up to 10% of the tax underpaid plus additional interest; failure to file after an official notice can trigger administrative assessment and criminal penalty for serious evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business Situation and Financial Statements Report (年度業務報告及財務報表申報)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Commercial Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after fiscal year end, i.e., by June 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit invites fines of TWD 10,000–50,000; continued non-filing can cause revocation of the company/branch registration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent CPA audit is triggered when paid-in capital exceeds TWD 30,000,000 (approx. USD 1,000,000) or annual net revenue exceeds TWD 100,000,000 (approx. USD 3,300,000), or when the company is listed/regulated; otherwise audit is voluntary.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan Financial Accounting Standards (TFRS) as local GAAP; IFRS is mandatory for public entities and optional for large private enterprises.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Company Act Art. 22-1, the company must annually submit the list of shareholders, directors, supervisors, managers, and beneficial owners to the MOEA before March 31. Changes during the year, including share transfers, are separately updated with the same authority within 15 days of the change; the annual report reflects the year-end status.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Shareholders' Meetings and Board Meetings

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 20% corporate income tax on taxable income; an additional 5% surtax generally applies to undistributed earnings of a profit-seeking enterprise retained without an approved business purpose.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Taiwan generally provides no broad corporate tax holiday for an ordinary market-entry consultancy. Qualifying enterprises may access R&D investment tax credits, specified innovation incentives, or other industry-specific incentives subject to statutory eligibility, approval, documentation, and anti-double-benefit rules. Small-enterprise reduced-rate rules may apply only where statutory capital, employee, income, and taxable-income conditions are satisfied.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Taiwan profit-seeking enterprise income tax return, generally Form 1101 for ordinary companies, filed through the National Taxation Bureau electronic filing system and the Ministry of Finance eTax platform. A company using an accounting year other than the calendar year uses the applicable annual return form and filing period prescribed for that accounting year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; provisional filing may be required for qualifying companies during the ninth month of the accounting year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year company, the annual income tax return and tax payment are generally due by the last day of the fifth month following year-end, normally 31 May. A provisional return is generally filed during the ninth month of the accounting year, normally 1 to 30 September for a calendar-year company, unless an applicable exemption applies. Extensions require statutory grounds or approval.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taiwan business administration number, legal name, registered address, accounting year, tax registration status, paid-in capital, and entity classification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Taiwan company's own registration and tax identifiers. Do not use the Chinese parent company's registration number unless the form expressly requests related-party information.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit or loss according to the audited or approved financial statements for the relevant accounting period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the Taiwan entity's statutory accounts. Revenue earned by the mainland parent or other foreign affiliate must not be included unless legally earned by, or allocated to, the Taiwan entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-backs and deductions for non-deductible expenses, exempt income, tax-exempt income, depreciation differences, provisions, related-party adjustments, entertainment expenses, donations, fines, and other statutory items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign taxes, withholding taxes, service fees, royalties, and management charges require supporting contracts, invoices, proof of benefit, payment evidence, and arm's-length substantiation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax depreciation, amortization, asset additions and disposals, useful lives, and book-to-tax differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-owned or leased assets used in Taiwan must be supported by ownership or lease documentation and evidence of Taiwan business use.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Use of prior-year assessed losses against current taxable income, subject to the statutory ten-year carryforward period and qualifying bookkeeping, filing, and assessment conditions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses of the foreign parent, another group entity, or an offshore branch cannot be deducted by the Taiwan company. Maintain assessment notices and loss schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party identities, relationship percentages, transaction categories, amounts, outstanding balances, pricing methods, and transfer-pricing documentation status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose transactions with the Chinese parent, affiliates, directors, shareholders, and common-control entities, including cross-border consultancy, cost-sharing, financing, royalty, and reimbursement arrangements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Taxable income and corporate income tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after statutory adjustments multiplied by the applicable corporate income tax rate, with available credits and prepaid tax deducted.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply Taiwan tax rules to Taiwan-source income and income attributable to the Taiwan legal entity. Foreign tax credit claims require qualifying foreign tax payment evidence and are capped by the Taiwan tax attributable to the relevant foreign-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation of the 5% surtax on current-year earnings retained after statutory adjustments, subject to permitted distributions, capital reinvestment, and other approved exclusions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Document dividend declarations, capital increases, qualifying investment, and business-purpose retention. A parent-company decision to retain profits does not alone eliminate the surtax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Withholding tax and provisional tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taiwan withholding tax suffered, provisional tax paid, and other permitted credits applied against the annual liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile all withholding certificates to the Taiwan entity's ledger and tax return. Withholding suffered by the parent cannot be credited by the Taiwan subsidiary.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Electronic signature, attachments, and payment confirmation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Electronic filing certification, financial statements, accounting records, transfer-pricing attachments where required, tax payment receipt, and supporting schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Retain bilingual or translated related-party agreements, board approvals, beneficial-owner information, and evidence supporting the commercial substance of the Taiwan operations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or failure to file may result in an administrative fine generally calculated by reference to the tax payable, subject to statutory minimums and maximums. Late payment generally incurs a surcharge of 1% for each two-day period of delay, up to the statutory maximum, followed by collection measures. Underreported or omitted income may trigger additional tax, penalties commonly up to twice the underpaid tax, interest, and possible criminal exposure for intentional evasion. Exact amounts depend on the assessment, filing status, cooperation, and applicable Tax Collection Act provisions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 21% on dividends distributed by a Taiwan company to a nonresident individual, foreign company, or mainland Chinese enterprise, subject to applicable special rules and any legally available relief. Dividends paid to a Taiwan-resident corporate shareholder are generally subject to Taiwan's intercorporate dividend rules rather than nonresident withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Taiwan's treaty network must be checked for the recipient's legal status and residence. Before payment, obtain a valid certificate of tax residence, beneficial-ownership and entitlement evidence, corporate registration documents, ownership information, treaty forms, and transaction agreements. Apply to the competent tax authority or withholding agent for treaty relief where pre-approval is required; otherwise withhold at the domestic rate and pursue the prescribed refund or adjustment procedure. The People's Republic of China and Taiwan do not have a conventional bilateral income tax treaty for ordinary cross-Strait payments; a Chinese mainland recipient should not assume DTA relief. Mainland investment, remittance, and tax-credit treatment must also be reviewed under the Cross-Strait Act and applicable regulations.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Taiwan domestic withholding is generally 20% on royalties and interest paid to nonresident enterprises, subject to statutory exemptions, special financial-institution rules, source rules, and treaty relief. Treaty rates differ by agreement and payment category and commonly require residence, beneficial-ownership, and limitation-on-benefits analysis. Payments to a Chinese mainland recipient generally require domestic-law analysis rather than automatic treaty reduction. Taiwan-source technical, consulting, installation, and service fees may also be subject to 20% withholding where the income is Taiwan-source or the services are performed in Taiwan; contract characterization alone does not determine source.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Taiwan local-file documentation is generally required where the taxpayer's annual net operating revenue and non-operating income reaches at least NT$300 million or the annual aggregate amount of controlled transactions reaches at least NT$200 million, subject to detailed exemptions and transaction-category rules. A master file is generally required where the Taiwan entity belongs to a multinational enterprise group meeting the applicable consolidated-revenue threshold, commonly NT$3 billion, together with the prescribed cross-border related-party conditions. Country-by-country reporting generally applies at the group level where consolidated revenue reaches NT$27 billion, subject to filing and notification rules. Exact thresholds and exemptions must be confirmed for the relevant fiscal year.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan applies substance-over-form, anti-avoidance, transfer-pricing, controlled foreign company, beneficial-ownership, and business-purpose principles. Taiwan does not operate a single offshore Economic Substance Regulations regime identical to the Cayman Islands or British Virgin Islands regimes; however, an entity must demonstrate real personnel, premises, decision-making, functions, assets, risks, records, and commercial purpose. A Taiwan consultancy invoicing the Chinese parent should evidence local staff, management control, client work, deliverables, market activity, and risk assumption. Artificial arrangements may be recharacterized, denied deductions, subjected to withholding, or treated as dividend or other taxable distributions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing Taiwan revenue, issuing false invoices, fabricating expenses, maintaining parallel books, or shifting consultancy profit to the Chinese parent without functions, assets, risks, or supporting evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Additional assessed tax, interest, administrative penalties that may reach twice the underpaid tax, invoice penalties, compulsory collection, and criminal prosecution for intentional tax evasion. Criminal penalties can include imprisonment and fines under Taiwan tax and criminal laws.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and responsible persons may face criminal liability, fines, civil restitution, tax collection against legally reachable assets, disqualification consequences, and travel or exit restrictions where legally ordered. Corporate limited liability does not protect intentional personal misconduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using unsupported cost-plus markups, excessive management fees, non-arm's-length royalties, interest-free financing, or profit allocation inconsistent with actual functions and risks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax authority may adjust taxable income to an arm's-length amount, deny deductions, impose additional corporate income tax, assess withholding tax, apply interest and penalties, and require local-file, master-file, or audit documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may incur civil liability for losses caused by knowingly approving non-arm's-length transactions, false records, or unlawful distributions; criminal exposure arises where conduct constitutes tax fraud, forgery, breach of trust, or other offenses.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Illegal profit repatriation and withholding failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties, interest, service fees, or disguised distributions offshore without withholding and reporting, or treating shareholder withdrawals as deductible business expenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Withholding agent liability for the unpaid tax, collection of tax from the Taiwan company, interest, penalties, denial of deductions, and possible additional 5% undistributed-earnings surtax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible persons may be jointly exposed under tax collection, company, and criminal laws for deliberate withholding failures, unlawful distributions, misuse of corporate assets, or false accounting.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company and lack of economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Taiwan company solely as an invoicing, treaty-shopping, payment-routing, or profit-parking vehicle without local personnel, premises, decision-making, deliverables, or commercial activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty or domestic tax benefits, recharacterization of income, transfer-pricing adjustments, withholding assessments, invoice penalties, beneficial-ownership challenges, and possible anti-avoidance reassessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil damages, breach-of-duty claims, personal tax or criminal exposure for fraudulent arrangements, and regulatory restrictions. Travel bans or imprisonment are not automatic and require statutory grounds and competent-authority or judicial process.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML, sanctions, and suspicious cross-border payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving or remitting funds without identifying the beneficial owner, using opaque intermediaries, splitting transactions, routing payments through unrelated accounts, or processing sanctioned or prohibited counterparties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transaction rejection, account suspension, suspicious-transaction reporting, asset freezing or seizure, administrative fines, and criminal penalties under Taiwan anti-money-laundering and sanctions-related laws.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and employees may face personal fines, criminal prosecution, asset confiscation, civil liability, and restrictions on leaving Taiwan where authorized by law. Corporate form does not shield knowing participation or deliberate failure to report.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting mainland capital, making payments, acquiring assets, or transferring technology without required approval, declaration, banking documentation, or compliance with Cross-Strait restrictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines, orders to rectify or unwind the transaction, confiscation or forced repatriation, remittance restrictions, license or registration consequences, and criminal liability for serious or intentional violations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and responsible persons may be personally liable for unlawful approvals, concealment, or unauthorized transfers and may face fines, criminal prosecution, asset measures, and legally ordered travel restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlawful corporate distributions and insolvency misconduct
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends from nonexistent profits, distributing capital while insolvent, paying related parties ahead of creditors, or disguising shareholder loans as expenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Repayment or restitution of the distribution, director liability for corporate losses, creditor claims, accounting penalties, tax reassessment, and criminal liability for breach of trust or unlawful distribution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face joint civil restitution, creditor damages, disqualification, asset execution, and imprisonment where the conduct satisfies criminal elements. Travel bans are case-specific and require lawful authority.
